person_note: Beth is the participating first-person narrator. The Goodreads evidence repeatedly places her inside scenes through “I,” “me,” “my,” and story-specific “we” across court, childhood, marriage, motherhood, bereavement, and later family material. The authorized opening independently confirms that voice, while whole-book and interior analyses identify Beth’s narration across the interwoven timelines. Universal “you/we” aphorisms, dialogue, and the dedicated poem are local or non-base material, not changes in controlling person. One quote has ambiguous missing speech boundaries, but it does not create a credible structural conflict; no sustained narration in another person was found.
